title: Body: a scan with your eyes open

outline.heading: Why attention to the body at all

points.text: The body gives what the breath cannot: scale.

outline.heading: The honest caveat that usually gets put at the end

points.text: With a history of trauma, prolonged uninterrupted concentration on bodily sensation is not a suitable format.
David Treleaven, Trauma-Sensitive Mindfulness (W. W. Norton, 2018)

In the sample of Goldberg, Lam, Britton and Davidson (Psychotherapy Research, 2022; 434 people with meditation experience), re-experiencing traumatic material is among the most frequent adverse effects, and adverse childhood events appear as a risk factor.
Treleaven's central notion is the window of tolerance.
The task is not to "finish the scan" but to stay inside the window, even if that means cutting the scan off halfway.

outline.heading: Four modifications that make the format safer

points.text: A fifth, separate one: movement as a way back.
No "working with the holding pattern", no "releasing trauma from the body", no "breathing into the pain".

points: The body gives you scale that the breath cannot.
If you have a history of trauma, prolonged uninterrupted concentration on bodily sensation is not a suitable format.
David Treleaven addresses this in Trauma-Sensitive Mindfulness, W. W. Norton, 2018.
Goldberg, Lam, Britton and Davidson studied 434 people with meditation experience in Psychotherapy Research, 2022.
Re-experiencing traumatic material is a frequent adverse effect and adverse childhood events are a risk factor.
Treleaven's central notion is the window of tolerance.
Your task is to stay inside the window rather than finishing the scan.
You may need to cut the scan off halfway to stay within the window.
